display.purpose: The name in the band, once, after the red caret; 1.35rem from 1024px.

display-desk.purpose: The name in the band from 1024px.

headline.purpose: A page's head in Literata (Books, Settings, Admin).

percentage.purpose: How far a book is read, set large on the Kobo's side; the % sign at 0.42em; Faint at 500 for 0.

percentage-card.purpose: The percentage on a book card below 1024px.

dialog-title.purpose: The title of Help; 1.25rem at 520px and below.

card-heading.purpose: The heading of a card, Getting started and Advanced.

book-title.purpose: A book in the list, in Literata.

book-title-details.purpose: The title at the top of Details.

body.purpose: Everything else; running text to 62ch to 64ch.

nav.purpose: The navigation bar under the thumb.

nav-desk.purpose: The navigation row in the band from 1024px, and Sync now on a desk.

mark.purpose: The first line of a status on Hardcover's side, in the mark's colour; Details.

label.purpose: Table heads, filter group names, a book card's field names; sentence case.

small.purpose: Facts, hints, the legend, the edition line, the foot.

fine.purpose: The independence sentence, the count on Sync now, a tag.

sign-in-code.purpose: Set large to compare by eye with what Hardcover shows.

site-headline.purpose: The site's one h1, fluid from 2.4rem to 3.8rem, beside the download card; its own ramp, large where the page is small.

site-section.purpose: A section's h2 on the site, fluid from 1.7rem to 2.6rem; also on a card.

site-figure.purpose: A step's number on a gradient card, 6rem to 9rem at -0.06em.

site-step-figure.purpose: A step's number on a photo step card, 4.5rem to 6.5rem, so that the photograph keeps its top half.

site-line.purpose: The one paragraph on a story card, 500, held to 34ch.

site-sure.purpose: The line under Download for Mac: what it reads, what it writes, that it starts as a dry run. On Flag on the download card, white on the close's scrim.

site-lede.purpose: The line under a heading, in graphite, 60ch; white at 92% on a card.

site-body.purpose: The site's body and a step's paragraph.

site-caption.purpose: Captions, the foot, a screenshot's caption, the version line; 62ch.

site-name.purpose: The name in the head, with the Name Caret before it.

site-nav.purpose: The page's places in the head, graphite; ink and underlined on hover.

site-photo-title.purpose: A photo card's heading in the sans at 800: the park card's and It never guesses a match. Not a book title.

site-facts.purpose: The paragraph under a photo card's heading, 1rem at 94%.

site-button.purpose: Download for Mac; 1.25rem on the download card.

site-sheet.purpose: The base of the drawn row, 1.0625rem at 1.4; everything in the sheet is in em of it, so the row scales as one.

site-sheet-title.purpose: The book's title in the drawn row, Source Serif 4 at 1.0625em, 600: the Book Face Rule's one place on the site.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Light only, under cards and the white cards above the list on a desk. none in dark.

shadows.name: cover
shadows.purpose: A book cover lying on the Kobo's side, in both lights.

shadows.name: small-cover
shadows.purpose: The 32px colour cover on Hardcover's side.

shadows.name: dialog
shadows.purpose: Help and Details, over a backdrop of rgba(10, 12, 14, 0.6).

shadows.name: lightbox
shadows.purpose: A large cover, over a backdrop of rgba(10, 12, 14, 0.88).

shadows.name: disc-ring
shadows.purpose: The ring of a white disc on the seam (green for up to date, ink for failed); a grey disc has inset 0 0 0 1px var(--edge). A ring, not a shadow.

shadows.name: site-lift
shadows.purpose: Site, light only: under the gradient and photo cards and the sheet; none at night and on the quiet cards. The cover in the sheet carries the tool's cover shadow. The app icon casts drop-shadow(0 10px 18px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3)) on the download card and drop-shadow(0 18px 30px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35)) on the cobalt card.

motion.name: ease-proof
motion.purpose: Expo ease-out for the strike, the write-in, the sync gauge and the disclosure chevron.

motion.name: strike
motion.purpose: The red strike draws across the old value.

motion.name: write
motion.purpose: The new value writes in from the left after its caret.

motion.name: row-stagger
motion.value: 70ms per row, up to the thirteenth row
motion.purpose: Each row's strike and write-in start 70ms after the row above.

motion.name: landed
motion.purpose: Coming back to a row after an action: a Blue Wash on the Kobo's side of it that fades.

motion.name: cover-in
motion.purpose: A large cover fades and grows in.

motion.name: disclosure
motion.purpose: The chevron of 'Paste a token instead' turns.

motion.name: sync-gauge
motion.purpose: While a sync runs, the band-red gauge under Sync now fills by transform: scaleX(var(--p)) as the books go out; scaled, never resized.

motion.name: sync-sweep
motion.purpose: While the count is not known yet, a 30% band-red segment of the gauge sweeps across by translateX.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion every animation and transition is off; a row you came back to keeps a steady wash, and the sync gauge whose count is unknown is a faint full line (opacity 0.35).

motion.name: run-drift
motion.value: 7, 11, 17pt/s (back, middle, front), scaled with the run
motion.purpose: Mac app, Covers only (the approved second authored motion): the three rows of the press run drift left; the front row moves one cover in about six seconds.

motion.name: run-stand
motion.value: exponential ease, 0.18s time constant; 3s hold after a move by hand
motion.purpose: Mac app, Covers only: a row eases to a stop while a cover in it is lifted, the keyboard is in the run, or the large cover or Details is open, and eases back after.

motion.name: cover-lift
motion.purpose: Mac app, Covers only: the cover under the pointer or the keyboard lifts, its shadow deepening.

motion.name: run-reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Mac app, Covers: under Reduce motion, and whenever the window is not visible, the run stands still and moves only by hand; under Reduce motion the lift does not grow and the large cover appears without moving.

motion.name: site-rise
motion.value: 0.7s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), 60ms apart by --i, from 18px below and transparent
motion.purpose: Site, once on load: the download card, the sheet and the three story cards rise into place in page order.

motion.name: site-strike-write
motion.value: strike (background-size from 0 1.5px) 0.5s at 0.9s; write-in (clip-path from the left) 0.6s at 1.1s, both cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)
motion.purpose: Site: in the sheet's row, the tool's own strike and write-in at the tool's timing, after the sheet has landed. The three story cards stand still.

motion.name: site-reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Site: under prefers-reduced-motion the cards and the sheet stand in place, the strike and write-in are off, and smooth scrolling is off.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: At 520px and below: a term in Details stacks over a 6.75rem term column, Help's terms go to one column, filter group names go above their chips, Help's title is 1.25rem.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: The first book and its mark on the first screen at 390 by 844: the page line and the band's 'N of M books syncing' step aside, the band's two facts side by side, Filter and Sort share one row.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Two book cards per row; the band's status in three columns with the two buttons under them, to the right.

breakpoints.name: one-column
breakpoints.purpose: The band at the top of the page with its own Help button, the navigation a bar under the thumb, filters behind one button, each book a card (the Kobo's part, the seam across with the mark at its right end, Hardcover's part below), 2.75rem controls.

breakpoints.name: desk
breakpoints.purpose: The band across the top, the page in one window height: the list edge to edge, the Kobo's side on the grey, the seam at 64%, Hardcover's side white to the edge; the list scrolls in its panel under a sticky head; a one-line foot.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: The tagline under the name and the third status fact in the band.

breakpoints.name: coarse-pointer
breakpoints.purpose: Everything operated is 2.75rem, chips, Help and the theme switch included.

breakpoints.name: site-phone
breakpoints.purpose: Site: the story cards lose their 22rem floor (the photograph keeps 17rem, its words padded 6rem above); the four step cards go to one column and lose their 26rem floor (a photo step 16rem, its words padded 5.5rem above); the Books page's night capture and the Details capture are hidden, the phone capture is at most 14rem wide from a 400w copy, and the Mac app shows the Overview alone.

breakpoints.name: site-stack
breakpoints.purpose: Site: the sheet's row stacks (the book, the two switches side by side with their names above them, the margin under a double rule on its top); the other tools' table stacks; the in-page links leave the head; the Mac app's icon stands above its words.

breakpoints.name: site-claim
breakpoints.purpose: Site: the claim in two columns, the headline and lede at 1.5fr beside the download card at 1fr; the story and the Mac app's pictures across; the screenshots on six columns. Below it everything is one column, the download card follows the lede, and the cards under What it does lose their 28rem floor (the photograph 18rem, its words padded 6.5rem above).

breakpoints.name: site-four
breakpoints.purpose: Site: the four step cards in one row on three shared rows (subgrid), the figures on one line; two by two below, the same.

gradients.name: plum
gradients.purpose: Site: Your computer in the story. Words at the foot, on the deep end.

gradients.name: teal
gradients.purpose: Site: Hardcover in the story. Words at the foot, on the deep end.

gradients.name: teal-list
gradients.purpose: Site: What it does; the lime is a strip at the head of the card, the heading white like every card heading, the list on the teal.

gradients.name: slate
gradients.purpose: Site: What it leaves alone, with Site Ink dark words in both lights.

gradients.name: scrim
gradients.purpose: Site: under the words at the foot of a photo card.

gradients.name: scrim-step
gradients.purpose: Site: the step cards (four slices of one photograph), the story's and the photograph under What it does, which carry a heading and a paragraph; the words are padded 11rem above (9rem on the story card) so that the top half stays photograph.

gradients.name: scrim-close
gradients.purpose: Site: the close, with the download on it; it spans the whole photograph, the words held to 46rem.

components.name: Button
components.description: The default control: white, a 1.5px Edge, ink words at 700; 2.375rem, 2.75rem below 1024px and under a finger.

components.name: Sync now, live (red fill)
components.description: Red only when the sync is live; its second line counts what it is about to send.

components.name: On the band (Refresh, Sync now in a dry run)
components.description: Outlined in the band ink: Refresh, and Sync now when nothing goes to Hardcover.

components.name: Story card (site)
components.description: The plum story card, Your computer: an h2 at 1.75rem over one paragraph of 500 held to 34ch, on the dark end of the gradient, 22rem tall. The same in both lights; it stands still.
components.html:
Your computer

The sync runs here, on your Mac or Linux machine. Its page shows what the next sync changes before anything is sent. No account with this project, no cloud of its own.

components.name: The drawn row (site)
components.description: The sheet: one row of the Books page drawn in the site's markup, with the tool's colours scoped to it in both lights, a 1px rule border and 18px corners; the legend of the four marks alone on the rail, the cover, title, gauge and facts, two drawn switches, and the margin with the caret, the strike and the write-in. The strike draws at 0.9s and the write-in at 1.1s, off under reduced motion.

components.name: Download card and the one button (site)
components.description: The one card that changes with the light: ink by day with white words, white at night with ink words; Download for Mac full width in the card's reverse, underlined on hover, the version line in Flag Quiet, the reassurance line in On Flag under it, brew and uv as code on Flag Code. Beside the claim from 900px, under the lede below it.
components.html:
Download for Mac

Version 0.19.0, 28 October 2026. A 12 MB disk image, signed and notarised; macOS 13 or later.

Reads your Kobo and writes nothing to it unless you ask. Starts as a dry run. Beta; Mac and Linux only.

Or in a terminal, on a Mac or Linux:

brew install merlijntishauser/tap/lastreaduv tool install lastread

components.name: List card with the marks (site)
components.description: What it does: the heading white like every card heading, on the tighter teal whose lime is a strip at the head of the card; the list on the teal with the page's tick as SVG in the words' colour, a 1.7rem mark column beside 1rem words.
components.html:
What it does

  • Sends status, progress and dates to Hardcover for the books you switched on.
  • Starts as a dry run: it shows what it would send, and sends nothing until you go live.

narrative.overview:
The page is drawn as the handover it makes. Every book has two sides: the
Kobo's, where it is read, and Hardcover's, where it is recorded. The Kobo's
side is grey e-ink paper: the book, a big figure of how far it is read,
the cover in greyscale, the Kobo's own dotted line of progress, and the
two switches, *Sync* and *State*. Hardcover's side is white, and there the
cover takes its colour. Between them runs the seam, an ink rule, and on the
seam each row carries its mark: what the next sync does with that book.
A reader who looks down the seam sees the whole handover at once.

The world is the two devices' own. The grey is the Kobo's screen, the
white is the web page that receives the book, the ink rule is the edge
where one hands over to the other. Above everything a dark band is the
tool itself: the name after a red caret, the navigation, what the Kobo and
Hardcover last did, and *Refresh* and *Sync now*. A quiet foot holds who
is signed in, the theme switch, Help and the sentence that says the
project is independent. Red is only for what a sync sends and the button
that sends it; blue is a question for the reader; a green tick is up to
date; ink is a failure and the reader's chosen filter. Everything else is
ink and grey.

It turns down the usual look for this kind of tool: a neutral list with
coloured status badges scattered across it. Status lives in one place, on
the seam, as a drawn mark with plain words beside it. Covers are the only
pictures, and the tool fetches them itself. The one authored motion is
kept from the earlier proofreading direction: when a value changes, the
old one is struck through and the new one writes in after a caret.

**The Mac app** (`packaging/macos/`) is drawn in Two Sides as well: the
dark band across the top of every pane, the Kobo's grey and Hardcover's
white with the ink seam between them and each book's mark on the seam as a
disc, in Books, Overview and Covers alike. Titles and the percentage are
Literata, in the window and the widget; controls and the words around them
are the system font, as a Mac app's are. Its colours are the page's tokens;
the few `mac-` tokens are only what macOS asks for beyond them (a red that
holds on a chosen row, the fill of a native button that sends, the stronger
values Increase Contrast takes). Its rules are the *(Mac app)* sections of
Components.

The site (`site/`) is a world of its own, kept apart from the tool's and
the Mac app's: the claim and the download, then one row of the tool's
Books page drawn at full size with the proof mark on it, on a white
ground by day and a near-black one at night, and under it the three the
sync runs between, the Kobo, your computer and Hardcover, one card each,
with photographs of people reading as cards too. It keeps its two faces
from its own font files, the page's marks, its one motion and its theme
switch, and the drawn row keeps the Galley Proof's colours. Its tokens
carry the `site-` prefix, the `site-sheet-` set and the three gradient
families, and its rules are under *The site* in Colors and Components.
keyCharacteristics: Two sides per book: the Kobo's on grey paper (`ground`), Hardcover's on white (`sheet`); the cover grey on one, in colour on the other.
The seam: a 2px ink rule between the sides, holding each row's mark as a 2rem disc.

Five discs on the seam: red filled with a caret (the next sync changes this), white with a green tick ring (up to date), blue filled with a query (needs a match), grey with a dash (not syncing, or nothing to send yet), white with an ink square (failed).
How far a book is read, set large in Literata at 700, beside its cover.
A dark band across the top holds the tool; a quiet foot closes the page.
Two typefaces with one job each: Literata for book titles, page heads and the percentage; Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for everything else.
Red only for what a sync sends: *Sync now* is red only when the sync is live, and outlined in a dry run.
Light and dark share every role; WCAG 2.2 AA in both.
One authored motion: the strike draws, the new value writes in.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Red fills only *Sync now* while the sync is live, and *Go live*, and marks only what a sync sends. In a dry run *Sync now* is outlined in the band's ink like *Refresh*, because nothing goes to Hardcover. Every other filled button is an ink fill (*Start using Lastread*, *Connect to Hardcover*, *I have approved it*, *Use*, a confirmation, *Check and save*). Blue is only for a question for the reader or the step they are on; a label that states a fact (*New*, *Admin*) is grey. A removing action is ink, never red. The site has no red fill at all: its one filled button is the card's reverse, and the sheet carries red as a mark only.

rules.name: The Seam Rule
rules.body: A row's status is said once, on the seam, as a disc with the mark in it and the words beside it on Hardcover's side. The legend, folded behind *What the marks mean*, holds every mark the seam can carry, drawn and coloured the same, with the words of the page's strings: *Next sync changes this*, *Nothing to send yet*, *Up to date*, *Kept as on Hardcover*, *Needs you*, *Failed*, *Not syncing*. Help explains each one under *Hardcover status*. A new mark is not used until it is in both.

rules.name: The Two Lights Rule
rules.body: Every colour has a light and a dark value with the same role. A colour that exists in one theme only is a mistake. In dark the red and blue are lighter and fills carry dark words (`on-fill-dark`); the band's colours are the same in both. On the site the gradient and photo cards are the same in both lights, a card does not change with the room; the ground, the words, the quiet card, the download card and the sheet swap, the download card from ink to white, so that the action stays the strongest thing on the ground in each light.

rules.name: The Legible Rule
rules.body: Words stand at 4.5:1 or more on whatever they are on, the edge of a field and every mark at 3:1 (WCAG 2.2 AA), in both themes. `tests/test_design_tokens.py` checks the pairs from `kobo.css`. The site's pairs are given under *The site* above; on a card the words stand on the dark end of the gradient, never on the bright stop.

rules.name: The Reading Face Rule
rules.body: Literata is for what is read as a book: book titles in the list, at the top of Details and under a large cover, a page's head, and the percentage. The name, sans headings, buttons, labels and every fact are Atkinson Hyperlegible Next. The Mac app keeps the rule in its own terms: Literata for book titles, the percentage and the heads of Overview's two sides, the system font for everything else. The site's drawn row keeps its own title face (`site-sheet-title`).

rules.name: The Figures Rule
rules.body: Tabular figures go only where numbers stand in columns or are compared: the percentage, the facts under a gauge (`.meta`), the counts on chips, the count on the Filter button, the end of the list's count, Getting started's tally and step numbers, the count on *Sync now*, and code. Never on the root or on running text. `tests/test_design_tokens.py` holds this.

rules.name: The Finger Rule
rules.body: Below 1024px fields, selects, buttons and *Details* are 2.75rem (44px), and the theme switch 2.5rem. Under a coarse pointer, at any width, everything you operate is 2.75rem, chips and the theme switch included.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are told apart by tone and a rule. A shadow is never needed to read the page; the dark theme proves it.

rules.name: The Round Means Something Rule
rules.body: A round shape on the page is one of three: a mark's disc on the seam, a filter chip (a pill), or a step number's circle. Buttons, fields, switches and tags stay square-cornered at 6px or 3px. The site's largest corner on anything you operate is 12px.

dos: **Do** put a book's status on the seam, as one 2rem disc with its mark, and its words beside it on Hardcover's side.
**Do** strike the old value in red and write the new value after a red caret when the next sync changes something.
**Do** fill red only *Sync now* while the sync is live and *Go live*; outline *Sync now* in a dry run, and give every other filled button the ink fill.
**Do** keep blue for a question for the reader, or the step they are on.
**Do** fill the chosen filter chip, the pressed theme button and any other chosen state in ink.
**Do** add any new mark to the legend and to Help's *Hardcover status*, drawn and coloured the same, before it appears on the seam.
**Do** show the cover in grey on the Kobo's side and in colour on Hardcover's.
**Do** set book titles, page heads and the percentage in Literata, and everything else in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next.

**Do** put `tabular-nums` only on numbers that stand in columns or are compared: the percentage, the facts, chip counts, the Filter count, the end of the list's count, Getting started's tally and step numbers, code.
**Do** use 4px for cards, book cards and dialogs, 6px for what you operate, 3px for small inner parts, and the 2px ink seam as the one heavy line.
**Do** make every control 2.75rem below 1024px and under a finger.
**Do** give every new colour a light and a dark value with the same role, and check it: 4.5:1 for words, 3:1 for field edges and marks; on the band use the band's own mark colours.
**Do** make every action work without JavaScript, and stop every motion under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** draw a missing cover as the crossed box.
**Do** keep the site's cards the same in both lights, the words on the dark end of the gradient; only the download card and the sheet swap, the card ink by day and white at night.
**Do** draw the site's marks as the page's caret, tick, circled query and dash, inline SVG: in the words' colour on a card, in the sheet's own red, green, blue and faint on the sheet.
donts: **Don't** scatter status as coloured dots or badges across a row; a book's status is its one disc on the seam, with plain words beside it.
**Don't** use red for decoration, for a warning, or for a button that removes something; a removing action is ink, underlined.
**Don't** use pill shapes for buttons, tags, fields or switches; the pill is the filter chip's, and the disc is the seam's.
**Don't** set `tabular-nums` on the root or on running text.
**Don't** set anything but a book title, a page head or the percentage in Literata.
**Don't** load Schibsted Grotesk or Source Serif 4 on the page; the Mac app takes Literata from the page's own files.
**Don't** rely on a shadow to separate surfaces; the dark theme has none.
**Don't** set labels in capitals or track them out.

**Don't** add a second authored motion; the strike and the write-in are the one. The Mac app's *Covers* pane is the one approved exception: the drift and the lift, standing still under Reduce motion and when not visible. The site's is its own one: the download card, the sheet and the story cards rise once on load and the strike and write-in follow in the sheet's row, standing still under reduced motion.

**Don't** load a font, a script, a style or a picture from elsewhere; the tool serves everything, the two fonts and the book covers included, and the site bundles its fonts and its four photographs. The site's one request out is the latest release's version, with JavaScript; without it the download link stands.
**Don't** put a kicker or an eyebrow above a heading, on the page or on the site, or a hairline between the site's cards; colour parts them. The site sheet's rules stay inside the sheet.
